literal: In a village with many roosters, morning comes late.
meaning: When too many people get involved in a job, it is hard to get a result.
equivalent: Too many cooks spoil the broth.

literal: When a tree has fruit, it lets its head hang down.
meaning: A knowledgeable person who does useful work is humble.
equivalent: The boughs that bear most hang lowest.

literal: Even if mountains come between, heart finds its way to heart.
meaning: Distance and obstacles cannot keep apart people who love each other.

literal: Whoever has no tracks in the field has no say at the harman (threshing-floor).
meaning: Nothing good comes from someone who does not put in the work and produces nothing.

literal: A cheese ship doesn't move with laf (talk).
meaning: Saying "I'll do this, I'll do that" does not get the job done.

literal: Stretch your feet according to your quilt.
meaning: Keep your spending within your income.
equivalent: Cut your coat according to your cloth.

literal: When the cart tips over, many people show the way.
meaning: Advice given when it is too late is worth nothing.
equivalent: It is easy to be wise after the event.

literal: While trying to imitate the partridge, the crow forgot its own walk.
meaning: Someone who tries to imitate what they admire and cannot manage it loses their own natural way too.

literal: On low ground, a little hill thinks it is a mountain.
meaning: Where there are no knowledgeable people, someone who knows little acts like an expert.
equivalent: Closest: a big fish in a small pond.
